issues.detail: The Greek 'ου μη τελεσητε' (ou mē telesete) is a double negative meaning 'you will not have finished' or 'you will not have completed'. The Vietnamese 'chưa đi khắp' (have not yet gone through/around) changes the tense/aspect from a future perfect negation (will not have completed) to a present/past perfective (have not yet). Specifically, the Greek implies a future completion point that will NOT be reached, whereas the Vietnamese sounds like a current state of incompletion.
